statement: The composition of two successive spatial rotations R_B and R_A represented by unit quaternions B = cos(beta/2) + B sin(beta/2) and A = cos(alpha/2) + A sin(alpha/2) yields the composite rotation R_C = R_B R_A with associated unit quaternion C = B A = cos(gamma/2) + C sin(gamma/2), where the composite rotation angle gamma is given by gamma = 2 arccos((1 - A . B) cos((beta - alpha)/2) + (1 + A . B) cos((beta + alpha)/2)) and the normalized rotation axis is C = D / (2 sin(gamma/2)) = D / ||D||, with unnormalized axis vector D = (sin((beta + alpha)/2) + sin((beta - alpha)/2)) A + (sin((beta + alpha)/2) - sin((beta - alpha)/2)) B + (cos((beta - alpha)/2) - cos((beta + alpha)/2)) (B x A).

steps.text: Represent spatial rotations R_A and R_B with rotation axes A, B and rotation angles alpha, beta as unit quaternions A = cos(alpha/2) + A sin(alpha/2) and B = cos(beta/2) + B sin(beta/2). The composite rotation R_C = R_B R_A has rotation axis C and angle gamma defined by the quaternion product C = B A = (cos(beta/2) + B sin(beta/2)) (cos(alpha/2) + A sin(alpha/2)).

Expand the quaternion product into scalar and vector components: cos(gamma/2) + C sin(gamma/2) = (cos(beta/2) cos(alpha/2) - B . A sin(beta/2) sin(alpha/2)) + (B sin(beta/2) cos(alpha/2) + A sin(alpha/2) cos(beta/2) + B x A sin(beta/2) sin(alpha/2)).

Equate the scalar part to the spherical law of cosines identity cos(gamma/2) = cos(beta/2) cos(alpha/2) - B . A sin(beta/2) sin(alpha/2), giving composite angle gamma = 2 arccos(cos(beta/2) cos(alpha/2) - B . A sin(beta/2) sin(alpha/2)), and extract the unnormalized vector axis D = C sin(gamma/2) = B sin(beta/2) cos(alpha/2) + A sin(alpha/2) cos(beta/2) + B x A sin(beta/2) sin(alpha/2).

Apply angle addition trigonometric substitutions to rewrite gamma and D: gamma = 2 arccos((1 - A . B) cos((beta - alpha)/2) + (1 + A . B) cos((beta + alpha)/2)) and D = (sin((beta + alpha)/2) + sin((beta - alpha)/2)) A + (sin((beta + alpha)/2) - sin((beta - alpha)/2)) B + (cos((beta - alpha)/2) - cos((beta + alpha)/2)) (B x A).
Normalize the composite axis vector D by removing sin(gamma/2) or computing its magnitude to obtain the unit rotation axis C = D / (2 sin(gamma/2)) or C = D / ||D||.

assumptions.assumption: A and B are unit quaternions representing pure 3D rotations with unit axis vectors ||A|| = 1 and ||B|| = 1.
assumptions.breaks_when: Quaternions A or B are unnormalized or axis vectors are not unit vectors, distorting composite rotation angles and axes.

assumptions.assumption: The composite rotation angle gamma is not a multiple of 2*pi (gamma != 2*k*pi).
assumptions.breaks_when: gamma = 0 or gamma = 2*k*pi (identity rotation), where the rotation axis vector D vanishes and the axis of rotation is not well-defined due to degeneracy.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero or indeterminate 0/0 when evaluating D / ||D|| or D / (2 sin(gamma/2)).
failure_modes.cause: gamma = 0 or gamma = 2*k*pi yields ||D|| = 0 and sin(gamma/2) = 0, reflecting that an identity rotation has no unique axis of rotation.

failure_modes.signature: Divergence or division by zero in tan(gamma/2) or individual tangent terms tan(alpha/2), tan(beta/2).
failure_modes.cause: The rotation angle equals pi (180 degrees), causing cos(gamma/2) = 0 and the denominator 1 - B . A tan(beta/2) tan(alpha/2) to evaluate to zero or diverge.
